newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia issues warning to demonstrators.
newsitem.headline: Serbia issues warning to demonstrators.

text.p: Serbia's Interior Ministry has said opposition political rallies will no longer be permitted if they obstruct traffic in breach of existing government regulations.

"The police in Serbia will not tolerate the blockade of traffic in future and warn the organisers of the demonstrations that they must exercise their right to peaceful demonstrations in keeping with the regulations," the ministry said in a statement quoted by the official news agency Tanjug late on Wednesday.
Observers said the statement's wording was so ambiguous that its immediate effect on continued opposition demonstrations planned for the centre of Belgrade on Thursday was unclear.

Opponents of Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic have blocked the centre of the capital for the past 36 days with massive protests triggered by the refusal of the ruling Socialists to acknowledge opposition victories in local elections.
The protests had been free of violence until Tuesday when surging crowds of pro and anti-Milosevic demonstrators clashed in the city.
Fifty-eight people were treated for injuries, including one man who was shot in the head and critically wounded.
West European states and the United States have warned Serbia that using force to obstruct the demonstrations would jeopardise rump Yugoslavia's standing with the West.
Earlier on Wednesday, one of the leaders of the Zajedno (Together) opposition coalition, Zoran Djindjic, said the authorities might be on the verge of banning future demonstrations.
He vowed at a news conference that the opposition would defy such a ban.
